mev-pbs.title: MEV & PBS (MEV-Boost) simulator
mev-pbs.description: Interactive simulator for MEV (sandwiching, backrun arbitrage), bundles/private transactions, and proposer-builder separation (PBS).

keyTakeaways.0: MEV comes from transaction ordering power, not just ‘high gas’.
keyTakeaways.1: Private bundles can reduce your sandwich exposure by hiding intent from the public mempool.
keyTakeaways.2: PBS turns MEV into a block-building auction: builders bid, proposers pick the highest bid.

stablecoin-depeg.title: Stablecoin Depeg Cascade
stablecoin-depeg.description: Simulate two depeg cascades: (1) collateralized stablecoin liquidations and liquidity drains, and (2) Terra-style algorithmic reflexive collapse.

keyTakeaways.0: Low liquidity amplifies price moves: the same sell pressure causes more slippage and faster depegs
keyTakeaways.1: Collateral crashes can trigger liquidations that sell collateral into markets, worsening the cascade
keyTakeaways.2: Algorithmic pegs can fail reflexively: redemptions mint supply, collapsing the backstop token and the stablecoin

wallet-tx-lifecycle.title: Wallet UX & Transaction lifecycle
wallet-tx-lifecycle.description: Simulate what happens when you click “confirm” in a wallet: nonces, EIP-1559 fees, mempool inclusion, replacement (speed up / cancel), and common revert reasons.

keyTakeaways.0: Your nonce enforces per-account ordering; a gap blocks later txs from being mined
keyTakeaways.1: With EIP-1559, you set max fee + priority fee; effective gas price is min(maxFee, baseFee + priorityFee)
keyTakeaways.2: Wallets check affordability using the cap: value + gasLimit × maxFee (not today’s effective price)
keyTakeaways.3: If base fee rises above max fee, the tx is ignored until base fee drops (or you replace it)
keyTakeaways.4: Speed up / cancel replaces the pending tx (same nonce) and typically requires a fee bump (≈10%)
